contentJudgment: The revised main argument is readable and largely faithful: anticipated danger, useful mobilization, cumulative costs, individual/social variation and context-sensitive coping. Essential and Core are coherent. Deep contains one unsupported specific causal explanation in rat-care that needs a local correction; no whole rewrite requested.

ru.title: Короткая разлука меняет последующий уход
ru.body: «Опыты с крысятами усложняют идею полезного раннего стресса. После возвращения детёнышей матери могут иначе заботиться о них; именно этот уход помогает объяснить дальнейшие различия».

en.title: Brief separation changes later care
en.body: “Rat-pup experiments complicate the idea of beneficial early stress. Mothers may care differently for pups after their return, and that care helps explain later differences.”

requiredFindings.issue: The screen supplies a separation → changed maternal care → later outcome mediation story as the book’s explanation. The cited growth chapter instead describes maternal deprivation/low care and an active-touch/growth-hormone experiment. Chapter 18 separately describes neonatal handling and more maternal care as producing similar beneficial outcomes; that passage does not establish changed maternal behavior after return as the mechanism of the handling effect. This is an unsupported causal bridge in this book account, not a claim that the mechanism is scientifically false.
requiredFindings.readerEffect: Readers receive a specific causal explanation of supposedly beneficial early stress that the represented source passages do not make. The current title repeats the added causal claim.
requiredFindings.minimalCorrection: Keep the screen and current human-transfer qualification. Retitle around active touch and replace the separation/reunion-mediated-care claim with the chapter-6 finding: separation lowers the pup’s growth-hormone measure; contact with a sedated mother does not restore it; simulated active maternal licking does. Alternatively describe chapter 18’s handling and maternal-care findings as separate observations without mediation, and update the source anchor to chapter 18. No extra screen or wholesale rewrite needed.

sourceLocator.section: «Постнатальный стресс»; «Механизмы, лежащие в основе стрессогенной карликовости»
sourceLocator.support: The active-contact paragraph compares separation, a sedated mother, and imitation of maternal licking; notes 138–139 discuss deprivation/maternal care.

sourceLocator.section: «Благополучное старение», neonatal-handling passage followed by «Но обычных крыс…»; note 503
sourceLocator.support: Handling and greater natural maternal care have similar positive effects; the author does not there identify increased care after reunion as the handling mechanism. This paragraph was cross-checked directly in the supplied original EPUB as well as the private extraction.

requiredFindings.acceptanceCheck: RU and EN title/body state only the selected supported book finding; retain animal-to-human limit. If a handling account is used, its source locator must point to the actual chapter-18 passage.

materialLimitations: Targeted primary passages across represented arguments, not continuous full-book reading or all-notes/scientific-literature certification.
Complete English edition was not collated; EN was reviewed against the represented RU primary meaning and the new RU condensation.

The required finding concerns support and attribution in this book, not a claim that the wider maternal-care mechanism is false. A matching exact primary-book passage would resolve it; an external fact should not silently substitute for the book.
Verdict applies to the hashed revised collector package; root reader at inspection still held 144 old pairs. Publisher owns integration/publication and browser/device QA.
